# Temperature devices These devices move [color=#a4885c]heat[/color] instead of gas, and are mostly used to cool engine loops or to keep a ship's coolant somewhere useful. They are not part of the standard air loop.
## Temperature gate The temperature gate only lets gas through while the gas on its [color=#a4885c]inlet[/color] side is colder than the temperature it is set to. Open its interface to set the threshold (from [color=orange]2.7 K[/color] up to [color=orange]4500 K[/color]), to switch it on and off, or to invert it so it opens on gas that is [color=#a4885c]hotter[/color] than the threshold instead.
Like the [textlink="pressure regulator" link="PressureRegulator"], the gate never creates a pressure difference of its own: it releases gas until both sides are at the same pressure, so it cannot push gas into a pipeline that is already fuller. It [color=#a4885c]requires power[/color] to run.
## Temperature pump The temperature pump moves heat, not gas. Its inlet pipeline is cooled down and its outlet pipeline is heated up, and it only ever works in that direction - the hot side has to face the cold side. Open its interface to set how much of the temperature difference is moved each second. It [color=#a4885c]requires power[/color] to run.
## Heat exchanger The heat exchanger brings the gas in its two pipelines to the same temperature without moving any gas between them. Hook the hot loop up to one side and the cold loop up to the other.
Do not confuse it with the [textlink="radiator" link="Radiators"], which exchanges heat with the air of the tile it sits on.
## Atmos meter The atmos meter is a gauge you bolt onto a pipeline. The length of its bar shows the pressure (up to about 6000 kPa), and examining it gives you the exact pressure and temperature. It is the quickest way to see what a pipeline is doing without carrying a gas analyzer.
